meta.title: OpenAI Agents SDK
meta.thesis: OpenAI Agents SDK is practical when learners can apply it to this concrete case: An OpenAI Agents SDK assistant resolves customer cases with tools and handoffs. By the end, they should be able to build or review Agents SDK design sketch with tools, guardrails, and handoff policy, measure tool success plus safe escalation rate, and catch the failure where a handoff fires without passing enough state to the next agent.

blocks.title: The SDK is more than a thin client

spans.text: Problem anchor: a tutoring product needs a KB-searching agent, a quiz-writing specialist, guardrails on output, session continuity, and traces for review. A direct model call is no longer the whole app.
The Agents SDK wraps the model loop with agents, runs, tools, handoffs, sessions, guardrails, and tracing in Python and TypeScript ecosystems.
If you do not need tools, handoffs, sessions, or traces, start simpler.

blocks.analogy: The Agents SDK is a production harness, not just a request wrapper.

blocks.title: Case study: tutor plus quiz specialist

spans.text: The tutor agent answers from KB notes. When the learner asks for practice, it hands off or calls a quiz-writer specialist. Tracing records model calls, tool calls, and handoff.
This is a good SDK fit because handoffs and trace inspection are product features.

items.text: Add specialist handoff only when routing is real.

blocks.title: SDK fit
blocks.prompt: When is the direct OpenAI SDK likely enough?

options.text: A multi-agent workflow with handoffs and guardrails.

blocks.explanation: Use the agent runtime when its primitives matter.

modules.title: Tools and guardrails stay application authority
modules.sub: The SDK routes calls; your app owns permission and validation.
objectives: Define function tools and hosted/MCP tools.
Apply validation and approval around tools.
Use guardrails for inputs and outputs.

blocks.title: A function tool is still your code

spans.text: A function tool exposes ordinary code through a schema so the model can request it. Hosted and MCP tools may broaden capabilities, but the app still owns credentials, authorization, idempotency, approval, and auditing.
Guardrails can validate or block inputs and outputs, but they should complement deterministic checks. Do not put secrets or broad tokens into prompts or traces.
Every side-effecting tool needs an approval and idempotency story.

blocks.analogy: The SDK can hand the model a phone; the app still controls which numbers can be dialed.

cells.text: Expose application code to the agent.

blocks.title: Tool authority
blocks.prompt: What must the app still handle for an SDK function tool?

options.text: Nothing; the model schema is authorization.
Authorization, validation, credentials, idempotency, approval, and audit.

blocks.explanation: Framework routing does not replace product security.

modules.title: Handoffs need ownership and return rules
modules.sub: Specialists should not create routing confusion.
modules.summary: A handoff is a workflow boundary.

blocks.title: Delegation and handoff are different shapes

spans.text: An agent-as-tool lets a manager call a specialist and keep control. A handoff can transfer the active task or conversation to a specialist. The product should decide which ownership model matches user expectations.
Handoffs need clear names, reasons, and return behavior. If a quiz writer takes over, should future questions return to the tutor? The state strategy must answer that.
A handoff should appear in traces with source agent, target agent, reason, and result.

blocks.analogy: Calling a specialist for advice is not the same as transferring the whole case.

spans.text: The tutor answers concepts. When the learner asks “quiz me,” it hands off to quiz_writer. After the quiz, control returns to tutor for explanation.
The trace records the handoff reason and final quiz artifact.

blocks.prompt: What should a handoff design specify?

options.text: Who owns the task after handoff and whether control returns.

blocks.title: One tool is enough for the first slice

spans.text: Start with one harmless lookup tool and one agent. Add specialists, sessions, and guardrails after the trace is clear.
Spaced recall: from choosing frameworks, prototype the risky path next, not a decorative multi-agent team. For OpenAI Agents SDK, that may be tool permission or handoff ownership.
Pin model and SDK versions in real projects because defaults can change behavior and cost.

blocks.title: Minimal OpenAI Agents SDK shape
blocks.code:
from agents import Agent, Runner, function_tool

@function_tool
def search_kb(query: str) -> str:
    """Search approved lesson notes for a learner question."""
    return "LangGraph is useful for explicit state, checkpoints, and interrupts."

tutor = Agent(
    name="Agentic AI tutor",
    instructions="Answer from the KB when possible and ask for clarification when underspecified.",
    tools=[search_kb],
)

# result = await Runner.run(tutor, "When should I use LangGraph?")
# print(result.final_output)
print(search_kb("LangGraph"))
blocks.explanation: The snippet shows SDK primitives while keeping the runnable part local. A live run would require configured OpenAI credentials and async execution.

options.text: Trace review, tool permission tests, output guardrails, and only then justified handoffs or sessions.

modules.title: Treat traces and sessions as production data
modules.sub: Continuation strategy and telemetry can create subtle bugs.
modules.summary: SDK conveniences need state and telemetry discipline.
objectives: Evaluate model, prompt, and tool changes.

blocks.title: State strategy is part of the design

spans.text: The SDK supports different ways to continue work: explicit histories, SDK sessions, or server-managed continuation strategies. Mixing them in one flow can duplicate context or lose constraints.
Traces may include prompts, user data, model outputs, and tool results. Treat them like production telemetry with retention, redaction, and access control.
A trace should help debug without leaking secrets or unnecessary PII.

blocks.title: Verify AI output from OpenAI Agents SDK

spans.text: Review the run trace and state strategy.

items.text: The agent used the intended model, instructions, tools, and guardrails.
Function tools validated permissions and arguments outside the model.
Handoffs have clear ownership and return behavior.
Session or continuation strategy is consistent for the flow.
Trace data is redacted, access-controlled, and used in regression evals.

options.text: They can contain prompts, user data, tool results, and model outputs.
